security_concerns.finding: The new undersized-terminal return hides every overlay, including pending permission details, but the event loop still dispatches approval keys. Below 60x12, y/a can approve an invisible request. This is newly introduced by the fallback; no dangerous actions were executed.

logic_errors.finding: Tab width is calculated before wrapping and not recomputed at column zero. At inner width 58, 55 ASCII a characters followed by tab and X produces a second row with three spaces then X, instead of the four-column tab stop implied by the helper. Caret advances to column 4 instead of 5.

A newline immediately after an exactly full row leaves a caret before that newline at col==width, then clamps it onto the last character. With width 58 and 56 a characters followed by newline and X, cursor_chars=56 renders at (row 0,col 57), on the last a rather than the insertion boundary. CJK at the boundary can put it on a continuation cell.

HEAD cursor movement is scalar-based, while the new renderer resolves positions inside a grapheme at its following boundary. For e + combining acute + X at cursor_chars=1, the caret is drawn after the accented grapheme, but inserting a character places it before the combining mark and changes what is accented. The isolated candidate does not inherit main grapheme-aware editing.

Combined live-tail row counts move a paged-up viewport on MessageUpdate: apply_with_scroll adjusts only committed logical-line counts. 100 history rows, 5 visible, offset 10 starts at 85; adding 20 live rows without committed lines starts at 105. The new live-tail accounting breaks frozen reading during streaming; logical-versus-screen-row drift is also inherited.

The newly used live-tail wrapper can emit over-width rows, which the unwrapped Paragraph clips. At wrap width 59 (60-column viewport), text "abc " followed by 60 x characters creates a first row of 63 columns, losing three x characters on display. The wrapper also excludes pending whitespace from its fit check. This is an inherited helper defect newly reached by live streaming, not corrected here.
